tasks.title: Package mocker as docker image
tasks.description: The working directory contains Hello/ - a complete, working QaaS mocker project (Hello.csproj referencing QaaS.Mocker + QaaS.Common.Processors Version=*; one-line Program.cs "QaaS.Mocker.Bootstrap.New(args).Run();"; hello.mocker.yaml serving GET /health -> 200 'ok' on Port 8080). Do NOT modify anything under Hello/. Create at the working-directory ROOT three files: (1) Dockerfile - multi-stage: stage 1 'FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build', WORKDIR /src, COPY . ., RUN dotnet restore Hello/Hello.csproj, RUN dotnet publish Hello/Hello.csproj -c Release -o /app/publish --no-restore; stage 2 'FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0' (CRITICAL: aspnet, NOT runtime - the mocker hosts an HTTP server and the runtime image fails at startup, FB s13#7), WORKDIR /app, COPY --from=build /app/publish ., ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "Hello.dll", "hello.mocker.yaml"]. Keep every Dockerfile comment on its OWN line - never inline after FROM/COPY/RUN/ENTRYPOINT (FB s13#18). The container listens on 8080 INTERNALLY (the seed default - do NOT change it). (2) docker-compose.yml at ROOT defining TWO services (see build-mocker-image skill section 9 for the exact compose shape): a 'redis' service that is INTERNAL ONLY (image: redis:7-alpine, with NO host port mapping - do NOT publish redis to the host; other services reach it as host 'redis' on 6379, and publishing 6379 would clash with a host service already bound to it, FB s13#19) and a 'mocker' service (build: . to build the Dockerfile above, ports ["8125:8080"] mapping host 8125 to the container's internal 8080 - ONLY the mocker is published to the host, depends_on: [redis]). (3) .dockerignore with at least bin/, obj/, *.md. The verify gate runs the real 'docker compose -p qaas-e03 up -d --build', curls host port 8125, then tears the stack down with 'down -v'.

verify.cmd: docker compose -p qaas-e03 down -v 2>$null | Out-Null; docker compose -p qaas-e03 up -d --build 2>$null | Out-Null; $body=''; foreach($i in 1..40){ Start-Sleep 1; $c=(curl.exe -s http://127.0.0.1:8125/health 2>$null); if($c){ $body=([string]$c).Trim() }; if($body -eq 'ok'){ break } }; docker compose -p qaas-e03 down -v 2>$null | Out-Null; if($body -eq 'ok'){ exit 0 } else { exit 1 }

acceptanceCriteria: aspnet:10.0 is used as the base image
failureModes: Using runtime:10.0 which has no HTTP host

goalOneSentence: Build and run containerized mocker compose-mocker-redis serving port 8125.
portContract: This is a docker-compose scenario. The mocker container listens on HTTP port 8080 INTERNALLY (the seed hello.mocker.yaml default - do NOT change it). docker-compose.yml publishes ONLY the mocker service: host port 8125 -> container 8080. The redis service is INTERNAL ONLY (no host port mapping - publishing redis 6379 would clash with a host service, FB s13#19; other services reach redis by service name). The live gate runs 'docker compose -p qaas-e03 up -d --build', curls http://127.0.0.1:8125/health expecting 'ok', then 'docker compose -p qaas-e03 down -v'. Do NOT change the mocker Port to 8125 - the container stays on 8080 and compose maps host 8125 to it.
